data.raw_text:
Finland’s president just said the trans-Atlantic relationship needs to be “salvaged.”
Salvaged.
Like pulling silverware from a house fire.
He’s right. But the person who set the fire isn’t Trump.
It’s the generation of European leaders who:
Shut down nuclear plants.
Banned fracking.
Heated their homes with Russian gas.
Let their militaries atrophy.
And spent thirty years riding American defense spending while lecturing us about our politics.
Britain has 25,000 reserve soldiers.
Finland — a country smaller than the Dallas-Fort Worth metro — has 280,000.
America produces 13.6 million barrels of oil a day. More than any country on Earth.
Europe can’t fuel a full work week. Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and the Philippines just moved to four-day weeks because they’re running out of energy.
The West hasn’t split.
The West has been exposed.
The people who built things are fine.
The people who didn’t are not.
Hope is not an energy policy. 🥃🦋
https://t.co/aqR01n0ByJ
